correctness.rationale: The monomial matrix gives injective, mutually orthogonal basis images, so each power has exact Calkin norm equal to a column-weight limsup. Gamma quotients and uniform endpoint control reduce this to an exact positive-ratio minimization, giving the square-root entry formula. Strictly positive matrix powers grow uniformly as the Perron eigenvalue; infinitely many rooted shifts with weights converging to its negative Bergman power prove non-Fredholmness throughout the disk, while the spectral-radius upper bound excludes its complement. The Hardy endpoint is separately treated with constant moment weights; the nonconstant block remains isometric.

originality.rationale: A comparison of exact mathematical implications shows that the inspected recent weighted Bergman polydisc results characterize boundedness or compactness, whereas the new claim determines all-power essential norms and two kinds of spectral sets for a specific strictly positive nonsingular toric semigroup. General weighted-permutation formulas provide a starting model, but do not supply the Perron-optimized closed forms and infinite-chain Fredholm argument without further analysis. Residual earlier-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: A much earlier weighted-permutation/shift-semigroup formula could implicitly imply the matrix-power expression without the identical terminology; a negative search is not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The exact entire essential-power sequence and simultaneous full Fredholm disk classify a natural toric bidisc composition family. The sharp Hardy/Bergman transition has dynamical meaning in operator-norm convergence, and the Fibonacci instance shows computable arithmetic power profiles. These questions are motivated by recent polydisc Bergman boundedness and compactness work, not arbitrary index sampling.
